events.title: Moon & Bloom — Showcasing East Asian Art at the BHS Castle
events.description: The Bayside Historical Society presents Moon and Bloom, a group exhibition featuring four New York–based artists — Beautiful_Soul, Jiae Kim, Dani Song, and Makoto Kishino — whose work draws on the enduring symbolism of the moon and the natural world, central motifs in East Asian art.Spanning painting, textile, and mixed media, the show gathers luminous moon jars, Korean folk painting (minhwa), shifting indigo textiles, and mixed-media "ecliptic moon" works into a quiet, contemplative garden where the cycles of nature and human imagination converge.Experience these works up close and meet one of the featured artists at The Castle in Fort Totten during the exhibition's two-week run this summer.EXHIBITION SCHEDULE:• Opening Date: Tuesday, August 4, 2026, 10:00 AM• Opening Reception & Demo: Saturday, August 8, 12:00–4:00 PM — enjoy light refreshments and an opportunity to meet the artists.• Artist-in-residence hours: Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, 10:00 AM–3:00 PM — Jiae Kim will be painting minhwa on-site in an open studio setting; visitors are welcome to observe and ask questions.• Closing Date: Friday, August 14, 2026, 3:00 PMAdmission is free. Get complete details at www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/moon-and-bloom-showcasing-east-asian-art-at-the-bhs-castle
events.location: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Queens Jazz Trail Concert: Wallace Roney Jr.
events.description: Experience the vibrant legacy of jazz in the heart of Queens this summer! Inspired by the iconic Queens Jazz Trail Map, this free concert series brings the borough’s rich jazz history to life in beautiful community parks—where legends like Armstrong, Coltrane, Fitzgerald, and more once called home. Presented by Kupferberg Center for the Arts, Flushing Town Hall, and Louis Armstrong House Museum in partnership with NYC Parks, the Queens Jazz Trail Concert Series honors Queens’ extraordinary jazz legacy and community spirit.MILES DAVIS CENTENNIAL CELEBRATION! Trumpeter Wallace Roney Jr. is a rising force in jazz known for his dynamic performances and deep connection to the tradition. The son of acclaimed artists Wallace Roney Sr. and Geri Allen, he was shaped by influences including Miles Davis and Freddie Hubbard before graduating from Oberlin Conservatory. Roney Jr. has performed with celebrated artists such as Chick Corea, Jimmy Heath, and Ornette Coleman, and is now a sought-after presence on the New York and New Jersey jazz scene.This concert will take place at Archie Spigner Park in Jamaica. It’s free—just show up! Bring a blanket, lawn chair, picnic, friends—even your dancing shoes—and join us for an evening of live jazz in the park!

events.title: Shakespeare in the Park "Macbeth"
events.description: Join NYC Parks, Hip to Hip, and the Friends of Cunningham Park for a free Shakespeare in the Park performance of "Macbeth" and "Kids & the Classics." This is a professional, family-friendly production offered to the public for free. The production is fully produced with sets, lights, wireless microphones for easy audibility, and sumptuous costumes. It will feature a professional company of actors courtesy of Actor's Equity Association. "Kids & the Classics" is a 20-minute pre-show, interactive workshop for children ages 4-12. It gives children a chance to interact with the text by previewing the story, and by creating links between the text and their own lives through theatre games and close reading of text.

Summer on the Hudson: Art in the Park
events.description: Art in the Park invites children ages 3-8 to learn about their local environment through a mix of arts & crafts activities. This hands-on, place-based curriculum builds kids' appreciation for the plants, pollinators, and wildlife found in Riverside Park, and fosters their creativity. Mondays and Thursdays at Camel Playground; Tuesdays and Wednesdays at Hippo Playground. Art in the Park is fully funded by proceeds from the Hippo Playground Spring Fair.

events.description: The Summer Sports Experience program participants receive age-appropriate instruction through organized clinics, skill stations, drills, conditioning, and live game situations led by experienced NYC Parks staff.

events.title: Summer Sports Experience: Basketball: Skills and Drills
events.description: Summer Sports Experience is an instructional youth program that teaches sports skills. Our knowledgeable NYC Parks staff train kids in sports such as basketball, ball hockey, kickball, flag football, pickleball, soccer, team handball, track and field, and volleyball. This program covers basic and more advanced techniques.  Summer Sports Experience is a drop-in program recommended for children ages 8-14. Participants can stop by for one or more sessions, but kids who stay for the whole program will get the most benefit from it. Occasionally a Summer Sports Experience program may be cancelled due to harsh weather or other conditions.Please note: We recommend that guardians accompany children participating in this program. Summer Sports Experience is not a childcare program, and NYC Parks is not responsible for the well-being of attendees. For more information, please visit nyc.gov/parks.  Contact accessibility@parks.nyc.gov or (212) 360-1430 for more information regarding accessibility.
